title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #4

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What do roots of cassava and sweet potato do besides taking in water? (1 mark)
   A. Store food
   B. Make leaves
   C. Make flowers
   D. Carry seeds

2. Frogs have smooth, wet skin and spend part of their life in water. They are (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Reptiles
   C. Amphibians
   D. Mammals

3. Which of these is a difference between plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. Plants die but animals do not
   B. Plants breathe and animals do not
   C. Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   D. Animals do not grow

4. Which of these is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Spider
   B. Ant
   C. Snail
   D. Hen

5. A goat lifts its head when it hears a noise. Which sign of life is this? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing out
   B. Reproducing
   C. Responding to changes
   D. Growing

6. Where does the digestive tube end? (1 mark)
   A. Gullet
   B. Mouth
   C. Stomach
   D. Anus

7. Which of these is a healthy habit for digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Never washing fruits
   B. Washing hands before eating
   C. Drinking water from a dirty pond
   D. Eating food that fell in dirt

8. What is absorption? (1 mark)
   A. Chewing food
   B. Passing faeces
   C. Swallowing food
   D. Digested food passing into the blood

9. Which of these is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Only soda
   B. Ugali, vegetables and beans
   C. Only sweets
   D. Only tea

10. Which part takes back most of the water from the leftover food? (1 mark)
   A. Gullet
   B. Stomach
   C. Large intestine
   D. Mouth

11. What does mass mean? (1 mark)
   A. How bright an object is
   B. The space an object takes up
   C. How hot an object is
   D. The amount of matter in an object

12. Which of these can be a solid, liquid or gas depending on conditions? (1 mark)
   A. Wooden chair
   B. Book
   C. Water
   D. Stone

13. What does volume mean? (1 mark)
   A. The amount of space an object takes up
   B. The colour of an object
   C. The amount of matter in an object
   D. How heavy it feels

14. At a wedding, what can organisers do to keep the place clean? (1 mark)
   A. Burn plastic
   B. Provide bins and clean after the event
   C. Throw waste in a river
   D. Leave waste on the ground

15. What is the danger of leaving plastic bags on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. They stay for a long time and block drains
   B. They grow into plants
   C. They turn into soil fast
   D. They make the soil rich

16. Where should a water conservation poster be put? (1 mark)
   A. Under a bed
   B. Near a tap or the school gate
   C. In a bin
   D. In a cupboard

17. Which of these helps farmers to save water? (1 mark)
   A. Flooding the field
   B. Drip irrigation
   C. Leaving canals leaking
   D. Watering at noon

18. Why do people spread ash or sand on a slippery path? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavy
   B. To make it hot
   C. To increase friction
   D. To reduce friction

19. Which force acts on a ball thrown into the air and brings it back down? (1 mark)
   A. Friction
   B. Sound
   C. Gravity
   D. Light

20. What is weight? (1 mark)
   A. The heat of an object
   B. The pull of gravity on an object
   C. The colour of an object
   D. The amount of light

21. A rolling ball slowly comes to a stop on the ground mainly because of (1 mark)
   A. Colour
   B. Light
   C. Sound
   D. Friction

22. Which of these will make a block slide the shortest distance on a ramp? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Oiled plastic
   C. Sandpaper
   D. Smooth tile

23. How does light travel? (1 mark)
   A. In curves only
   B. In circles
   C. In zigzags
   D. In straight lines

24. Why is it better to use daylight than electric light in the day? (1 mark)
   A. It makes rooms dark
   B. It is unsafe
   C. It costs more
   D. It saves money

25. Which of these materials passes heat quickly? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Metal
   C. Wood
   D. Dry cloth

26. What should you never do with oil that is on fire? (1 mark)
   A. Move away
   B. Call for help
   C. Cover it with a lid
   D. Pour water on it

27. Why do we boil water before drinking if it may be unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Heat removes all salt
   B. Heat makes water heavy
   C. Heat kills germs
   D. Heat makes water sweet

28. Why are cooking pots made of metal? (1 mark)
   A. Metal does not get hot
   B. Metal is light
   C. Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   D. Metal is soft

29. What should you use to hold a hot cooking pot? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bag
   B. Wet cloth
   C. Bare hands
   D. Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth

30. What is the source of heat that dries fish in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. A jiko
   B. A torch
   C. Electricity
   D. The sun

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why friction can be both useful and a problem. Give two examples of each. (4 marks)

32. Name two ways of lighting a house during the day. (2 marks)

33. A pupil grows two bean seedlings. One is put in a cupboard and the other in the sunlight. Both are watered. After a week the two look different. Describe what she might see and give a reason. (4 marks)

34. Make a plan for keeping your digestive system healthy for one week. (5 marks)

35. A jug has 1 litre of juice. 350 ml is poured into a cup. How much is left in the jug? (3 marks)

36. Describe safety measures to be observed when handling heat at home and at school. (5 marks)

37. Explain why deworming is important and state two other ways of preventing worms. (4 marks)

38. Discuss how the three Rs can be used for waste from a school kitchen. (5 marks)

39. Why is chewing food well important? (2 marks)

40. Explain the importance of heat in daily life. (5 marks)

41. Explain how ball bearings help a bicycle move. (4 marks)

42. Explain how farmers use light to discourage pests and animals. (4 marks)

43. Explain the difference between reducing and reusing water. Give one example of each. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Store food
   These roots store food for the plant.

2. C — Amphibians
   These features describe amphibians.

3. C — Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   Most animals move about and eat food, while plants make their own food.

4. D — Hen
   A hen is a bird and has a backbone.

5. C — Responding to changes
   The goat responds to a change in its surroundings, a sound.

6. D — Anus
   Waste leaves the body through the anus.

7. B — Washing hands before eating
   Clean hands prevent germs from entering the mouth.

8. D — Digested food passing into the blood
   Absorption means digested food parts pass into the blood.

9. B — Ugali, vegetables and beans
   A balanced meal has energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.

10. C — Large intestine
   The large intestine takes back water.

11. D — The amount of matter in an object
   Mass is the amount of matter in something.

12. C — Water
   Water can be ice, liquid water or steam.

13. A — The amount of space an object takes up
   Volume is the space a substance takes up.

14. B — Provide bins and clean after the event
   Bins and cleaning keep the place tidy.

15. A — They stay for a long time and block drains
   Plastic bags stay for years and block drains.

16. B — Near a tap or the school gate
   Posters should be seen by many people.

17. B — Drip irrigation
   Drip irrigation gives water directly to roots.

18. C — To increase friction
   Rough material improves grip.

19. C — Gravity
   Gravity pulls the ball to the ground.

20. B — The pull of gravity on an object
   Weight is the pull of gravity on a thing.

21. D — Friction
   Friction between the ball and the ground slows it.

22. C — Sandpaper
   Rough surfaces have the most friction.

23. D — In straight lines
   Light travels in straight lines.

24. D — It saves money
   Sunlight is free.

25. B — Metal
   Metals pass heat easily.

26. D — Pour water on it
   Water on burning oil spreads the fire.

27. C — Heat kills germs
   Boiling kills many germs.

28. C — Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   Metal passes heat from the fire to the food.

29. D — Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth
   Gloves stop heat reaching your hand.

30. D — The sun
   Sun heat dries fish.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Useful: brakes stop bicycles and shoes grip the ground. A problem: it wears out tyres and makes machines hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it helps in some cases and harms in others, and 1 mark for each correct example up to 3.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Windows and translucent roof sheets (skylights).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant in the cupboard looks weak and pale and the one in the light is green and healthy. Plants need light to make food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for describing each plant and 2 marks for the reason.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan including brushing teeth twice a day, eating fruits and vegetables, drinking clean water, washing hands, chewing well, deworming as advised and limiting sweets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible action up to 5.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 650 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 1 litre = 1000 ml, 1 mark for the subtraction 1000 - 350 and 1 mark for the answer.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Do not play with matches, keep children from fires, use gloves, turn handles inwards, switch off cookers and irons, keep fuels away from fire, cool burns with water and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure up to 5.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Worms live in the intestines and take food and make us weak. Deworming kills them. Wear shoes, wash hands, keep nails short.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 1 mark each for other ways.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: cook and serve only what is needed. Reuse: use empty oil tins for storage and sacks for carrying. Recycle: sell scrap metal and paper, compost peelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each R, 1 mark for one clear example and 1 mark for the compost point.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: It breaks food into small pieces and makes digestion easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for small pieces and 1 mark for easier digestion.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Heat keeps us warm, cooks food, dries clothes and crops, helps plants grow, makes rain by evaporation, and is used to make metals and glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 5.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are small steel balls in the wheel. They roll between moving parts, so there is less friction and the wheels turn easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what they are, 1 mark for rolling, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for wheels turning easily.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: They use bright or flashing lights at night near fields or animal pens to scare wild animals away. Lamps near sheds help to see thieves or pests.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bright lights, 1 mark for scaring away animals and 2 marks for examples.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reducing means using less water, for example closing the tap. Reusing means using the same water again, for example using washing water for the garden.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for examples.
